title: A new climate model PPE emulator that enables new insights on host model behavior
code_availability: A GitHub repository and manuscript are linked via QR codes in the presentation slides, but exact URLs are not printed in readable text.
testbed_rationale: This document is a conference slide deck; although perturbed parameter ensembles are valuable for emulation testbeds, exact dataset links, formats, and storage locations are not provided in text.
pain_points: Parameter interaction and non-linearity: Simple linear regression fails to capture higher-order parameter interactions and non-linear relationships.
Curse of dimensionality vs sparsity: Climate model PPEs typically have only a few hundred members, creating data sparsity in high-dimensional parameter spaces.

Variable grouping tradeoffs: Emulating all variables at once with neural networks overlooks isolated parameter-output relationships (e.g., TIWP and vf_mults), whereas emulating single variables one-at-a-time ignores inter-variable dependencies.
Impact of outliers: Outliers in PPE outputs strongly impact training and validation metrics but represent valid model behaviors rather than errors.
Cumulative impacts: Less individually sensitive parameters cumulatively have a non-negligible impact on model target outputs.
extraction_notes: Extracted from presentation slides. The slides note an alternative/original title: 'detecting and identifying the impact of parameter interaction on climate model outputs based on two Perturbed Parameter Ensembles (PPEs)'. Target variables include global and zonal averages (SW_CRE, precipitation, TIWP) and model skill scores against observations.
